author: ohtadmin
title: Trump halts Revolution Wind again
text:
The Trump administration said it is halting leases for five offshore wind projects under construction along the East Coast due to national security risks.
The Revolution Wind project, which is 15 miles from the southern shore of Rhode Island, is among those leases being stalled. The wind farm is 85% complete.
The Interior Department paused the projects Monday due to reports that have “long found that the movement of massive turbine blades and the highly reflective towers create radar interference,” which poses a national security risk.
Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said the action “addresses emerging national security risks, including the rapid evolution of the relevant adversary technologies, and the vulnerabilities created by large-scale offshore wind projects with proximity near our East Coast population centers.”
The “clutter” caused by these wind farms “obscures legitimate moving targets and generates false targets in the vicinity of the wind projects,” he added.
The pause will allow the U.S. Department of Defense “time to work with leaseholders and state partners to assess the possibility of mitigating the national security risks posed by these projects.”
A previous stop-work order by Trump on the Revolution Wind project was overturned by a federal judge in September.
The congressional delegation that represents Jamestown is condemning President Donald Trump this decision. U.S. Sen. Jack Reed, a Jamestown resident who serves as the ranking member of Senate Committee on Armed Services, said Trump’s policies have led to energy bills for the average American family increasing by 13% since January.
“President Trump’s outdated energy policies are killing good-paying union jobs,” he said. “While energy prices are soaring and our competitors across the globe are racing to innovate and find new sources of clean energy, we need to make energy more affordable and our energy grid more resilient. But Trump’s repeated attacks on offshore wind are holding our nation back, increasing energy bills, and hurting our economy.”
Congressman Gabe Amo said Trump’s “attacks on Revolution Wind are not based on science and facts. The administration is putting forward disingenuous arguments about ‘national security’ to try to kill this project simply because Donald Trump doesn’t like offshore wind. I will keep fighting to make sure this project is completed. We must deliver more affordable energy and a greener future for all Rhode Islanders.”
U.S. Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, who is the ranking member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, said Revolution Wind “was long ago thoroughly vetted and fully permitted by the federal government, and that review included any potential national security questions.” He said the move “looks more like the kind of vindictive harassment we have come to expect from the Trump administration than anything legitimate.”
“This is President Donald ‘Stop Work’ Trump trying to keep affordable, clean energy off the grid, without a care about how many working people have to lose their jobs to keep his fossil fuel billionaires happy,” Whitehouse added. “The Ocean State knows the great potential of offshore wind for our economy and environment. I will continue fighting to ensure these projects can move forward to help lower energy bills for Rhode Islanders and create more jobs and more opportunity for all.”
